requirement: Build a click command group whose subcommands share one inventory object through the context, saving it when the command finishes.
skeleton: An Inventory class and a click group with add, remove and list subcommands using ctx.obj, make_pass_decorator and call_on_close.
caption: An inventory command-line tool built with click, json and pathlib. The cli group takes a required --store path that can also come from INV_STORE and a --verbose flag, puts an Inventory object on ctx.obj and registers its save with ctx.call_on_close. Subcommands receive it through click.make_pass_decorator: add takes a quantity typed click.IntRange(min=1) and accumulates, remove raises click.ClickException for an unknown item, and list prints sorted tab-separated lines; verbose notes go to stderr. The fixture asserts accumulation and persistence, the quantity usage error, the environment variable, the ClickException and stderr output.

constraints: The store path is required and can be read from INV_STORE
Quantities below 1 are a usage error
Removing an unknown item raises ClickException with exit code 1
Changes are saved when the context closes

rationale.teaches: Create the shared object in the group callback, expose it with make_pass_decorator and persist it with ctx.call_on_close.
rationale.why: Subcommands that each build their own state or never flush it lose writes and make click groups hard to test.

ops.docstring: An inventory CLI whose click group shares one store object via ctx.obj.

candidates.why_wrong: The inventory is never saved, so every change is lost when the command exits.
A zero quantity is accepted instead of failing as a usage error.
The store path can no longer be supplied through INV_STORE.
Removing an unknown item crashes with KeyError instead of a clean ClickException.
Verbose messages are written to stdout and pollute machine-readable output.
